confidence_notes: Food and drink prices come from aggregated cost-of-living data found by web search: Numbeo (Nov 2026), Expatica, World-Prices and Expatistan. Numbeo gives about $20 for an inexpensive meal, about $80 for a mid-range meal for two and about $6.09 for a cappuccino. Expatica gives $5.67 for a cappuccino and $7.25 for a domestic draught beer. Numbeo puts domestic draft beer at about $7, with a $5-9 range. I set the mid-range meal a little above $80 because the July 2026 pricing window falls in tourist season. These figures do not include tax or tip. The cocktail figure is less certain. Expatistan lists $16 at a downtown club but calls it a guess based on few data points, and individual bar menus suggest $12-16 at full price. I picked a middle value of about twice the beer price. The wine figure comes only from individual venue menus showing $9-13 a glass, not from a citywide index. Accommodation figures are my own estimates from general knowledge of Denver's small hostel market and summer hotel demand. I did not search for accommodation or check booking sites. They are less certain, and real prices could swing about 25-35% with events and seasonality.
comparable_city_reasoning: I compared Denver with other mid-to-large US cities that have strong summer tourism. Numbeo's city comparisons place Denver restaurant prices about 25% below Los Angeles and about 22% below New York. Denver has few hostels, so dorm and private hostel prices follow other US cities with similar hostel markets. Summer hotel rates in central Denver are high because of conventions and mountain tourism.
